title: What If You Fell Into a Black Hole? It Depends on the Size

scenes.text: What if you fell into a black hole? The size decides everything.
Fall into a small one, up to about thirty Suns, and tidal forces tear you apart before you reach the edge.
Fall into a giant one, millions of Suns heavy, and you cross the edge feeling nothing. NASA's simulation takes about three hours to get there.
To anyone watching, you'd seem to freeze at the edge. Early astronomers called black holes frozen stars.
Inside, there is no way back. In NASA's simulation of a 4.3 million Sun black hole, stretching begins about 12.8 seconds later.
The last 128,000 kilometers pass in the blink of an eye. The start feels calm. The end doesn't.
